title: My UI works fine, but people see the AI look and stop right there
author: goddamnclever
selftext:
Im a senior full stack dev and i built a browser strategy game with AI. I designed all the mechanics myself and honestly enjoyed that part a lot, and i put real time into the architecture, the security layers and bot detection, all the parts nobody ever sees. I set the structure, the AI wrote the code. That side i am happy with.

The problem is the UI. Or more precisely what people think when they look at it. The moment somebody feels that an AI made this screen, the game gets the ai slop label and thats where the conversation ends. Nobody gets far enough to see what the game actually does.

And to be clear im not talking about broken UX. Everything works, the icon set is consistent, pages behave the same way, spacing does not jump around. It is not a mess. But i keep seeing games that look like 2005 and are half broken getting way more respect than something that works and looks modern.

What surprised me most is the gap between where i put my time and what people actually judge. Months on mechanics, balance, architecture, anti automation. Players decide in about four seconds and they decide from the interface.

So the question for this sub. When you design UI with AI, how do you keep the AI signature out of it? What do you actually do and which tools do you use? We built the frontend with tailwind and i suspect part of the problem is exactly that, everything defaults into the same shapes, the same rounded cards, the same spacing rhythm.

comments.author: SimCFB
comments.body:
You're targeting the wrong crowd. Most people don't give a shit. But some people make it a point to let the whole world know how much they do. 

I have noticed that a lot of AI interfaces look eerily similar. As if the models were trained on a set of looks and tend to prefer them.

Honestly I would just try different layouts. Astra is especially good at switching things up. Do that until you land on one that doesn't have that AI look and feel. It's a hell of a lot cheaper to redesign nowadays than it was before.

replies.author: goddamnclever
replies.body: you are right that most players dont care, the problem is where the loud ones sit. they are in exactly the subs where a small game gets discovered, so it is not only noise for me, it costs reach. and about the trained look, i think its less the layout and more the palette plus the same rounded card rhythm repeating on every screen. i will try the switching layouts approach, thanks.

replies.author: Heliaxx
replies.body: I think the bigger problem is just the images rather than the layout itself. That is the signature AI look. You could easily just replace it with some normal pictures I think? These aren't some hyper specific things, you don't even have to go through the trouble of regenerating the images with some prompts that give them a more distinct style (which can be done too)

replies.author: Dear-Jeweler5437
replies.body: We’ll be honest lol, this isn’t even your game this is a direct ogame rip off. That puts me off being interested to begin with and then the ai vibe on top makes it worse.

replies.author: SimCFB
replies.body:
Hah!

For one of my projects I was thinking of making a travian clone. But for WW2 with totally different mechanics (tanks and artillery etc). However... It did dawn on me that if active Travian players were to be my target audience. I would want it to look and feel a lot like Travian. Enough to where it would be clearly a different game. But close enough to make them feel at home. Cause us Travian players spend a RIDICULOUS amount of time in that interface.

replies.author: Dear-Jeweler5437
replies.body:
Go for it imo, if it’s a game you and other people like. 😊

I didn’t call out OP cos I’m anti ai or anti building on existing ideas, I just think it’s pathetic to 1:1 clone and claim it’s yours. But I’d totally play a ogame like game again if someone made a good one.

replies.author: goddamnclever
replies.body: mechanics and generic names are not something anybody owns. metal mine and shipyard are descriptions, not inventions, every game in this genre uses them. yes the core loop is ogames and thats the genre, the same way nobody calls a soulslike a rip off. what i built on top of it is not in ogame though, co-op pve invasions, officers you level up and trade with other players, a boss event, asteroid mining. you can dislike all of it but it is not a copy paste. and honestly this kind of surface level reaction is what kills my motivation, not the criticism itself

replies.author: Dear-Jeweler5437
replies.body:
Even a name such as sensor phalanx? A core ogame mechanic? That just shows 0 creativity on your end, what is different about your game.

https://ogame.fandom.com/wiki/Sensor\_Phalanx

Metal mine, crystal mine are fine but come on you even copied deuterium. Of every single building in your image not a single one is not in ogame lol.

replies.author: goddamnclever
replies.body:
phalanx itself, in my game it is not just a fleet scanner. that one building drives three separate ranges. one for scanning fleets like in ogame, one that decides which pirates show up on your pirate map, and one that decides which asteroids you can see and mine. so its level gates two entire mechanics that do not exist in ogame at all. same name, different job. and there is also a sensor disruptor building that degrades enemy phalanx scans on your planet.

the rest that is not in ogame:

\> alien invasions, a co-op pve event where npc fleets attack players and your allies can fly in and defend with you

\> commanders, officers bound to a ship type that you find on expeditions, level up with combat xp and sell to other players on an anonymous market

\> governors, same idea but for planets

\> an academy with skill trees instead of ogames flat paid officers, 7 trees and you spend your points where you want

\> pirates as static pve targets, plus a pirate king boss that spawns with a limited lifetime

\> asteroid mining, deposits you can only see inside your phalanx range, you park a fleet there and extract over time

\> parallel research queues, one more lane for every 200 total lab levels

\> combat, flight and cost simulators built into the game so nobody needs third party tools

\> temporary bonuses that spawn on random systems for 24 hours, so expeditions are not always the same value everywhere

\>deep spy, an espionage mission that stays over the target and keeps sending reports, with the detection risk going up on every one

thats the short version. if any of it sounds interesting i can send you the link ❤️

replies.author: account009988
replies.body: Standard first UI results. Everyone knows this is ai

replies.author: oadephon
replies.body:
It's not just the AI images. Look at it, it's just a grid of pictures. If you don't have a UI sense yourself, then at least have Claude Design look at it. Ask it to suggest some wild changes to your UI, entire overhauls to each screen and how they fit together.

People would've accepted a grid of pictures 5 years ago. Now, a UI needs texture, dimension, physicality, purpose, beauty. And the funny thing is that AI can still help with all of those! Ask it to make you a prototype with some layers and dimensionality, and see what it comes up with.

comments.author: Heliaxx
comments.body: Just make that portion yourself. Don't you have any vision on how you'd like it to look? Take some inspiration and create it yourself. To me the antis are way too dogmatic, but not being particularly fond of generic AI looking posters and GUI, I get that because I have it the same. Simply try to look at some competitor games UI that works and doesn't get this response and get inspired, it has to have some identity to it.

replies.author: goddamnclever
replies.body:
honestly the AI is already giving me exactly what i ask for. proper, consistent, nothing broken. and thats also what i look at when i play a game myself, spacing, pages behaving the same way, icons matching each other. as a developer what else am i supposed to look at :D   
  
but yeah, im not an artist and my vision on that side is probably not great.

replies.author: Heliaxx
replies.body: From the example you posted the actual UI ain't anything crazy but I don't think it's the problem. The generic looking AI images are the actual problem if I had to guess.

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body: Then why not just distribute the prompts you used so others can recreate it? If you didn't bring any personal contribution but just "directed" the AI why should anyone care and not just create their own version?

comments.author: TonyDaDesigner
comments.body: I think you're jumping to conclusions.

comments.author: Bubbly-Trainer7173
comments.body: Don't worry, **The "AI slop" we see today will be indistinguishable from human-made images in two or three years.**

replies.author: cowman3456
replies.body: Maybe quicker than that, if artists meet them halfway by striving to make their art look not-AI.  Lol.

replies.author: AvengerDr
replies.body: And if it doesn't? Are you prepared for that? Don't bank your whole personality on it.

comments.author: Scary_Objective6718
comments.body: Your framing suggests you may not be aware of this, but it's very likely your UI is simply bad, and attributing people's negative reaction to them recognizing the "AI look" sounds more like a narrative than addressing the root cause. I speculate this based on the wording of your post, and also because almost every UI I've seen designed primarily by AI has been poorly designed. Solve this by designing the UI/UX yourself first, with an actual mockup in something like Figma, then use AI to implement the design rather than having AI make the design decisions.

replies.author: ThatOtherOneReddit
replies.body: Another thing is 'AI' UI if you don't retheme is kinda noticeable since they all like that navy blue background with yellow elements for some reason.

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
I think your mistake is letting the AI "design" the UI.

Art and design is always going to be people's first impression of a game. As soon as there's even a hint of AI it's going to put a lot of people off.

If you have absolutely no art or design skills maybe look into trying to team up with someone that has. 

If you can do it yourself then take a look at sites like: https://www.gameuidatabase.com to get some inspiration.

Unless your game is full of bugs or has bad performance no one is ever going to know or care about the code but people will always care about the  look of it.

comments.author: AlgaeNo3373
comments.body:
I spent yesterday in UI hell iterating/refining a UI panel for a long time trying to wrangle it into useable state, let alone one that looks great. It's really challenging AI or no. 

One thing I hoped would work was prototyping it up in html first, locking in little features/functions/aesthetics. But translating that via Claude Code into Godot was a many-steps process.

replies.author: oadephon
replies.body:
You can use the design skill in Claude Code now. It will create prototypes in Claude Code and be able to view your code base, and then Fable can more or less flawlessly translate it to Godot in my experience. 

Having to jump back and forth between Claude Design and Claude Code was awful, no need for that anymore.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body:
Use graphical elements. Don't let an llm go and design your UI or it's going to make it look like a website, using CSS front-end standards and overfitted tailwind habits instead of designing for a game. 

If you're not capable of coming up with designs, mock some up on a visual model instead. Or go to the game ui database to look for inspiration.

UX is not as important as UI in games. That sounds silly to say, as someone who has been a web dev for 20 years. However when a game like Persona 5 gets rave reviews for its UI, you know that people care about the presentation more than the usability (not knocking on anyone here... the game is beautiful and I fucking love the feeling of its UI even after I've opened a screen a thousand times... but it is not remotely legible or intuitive from a UX perspective.)

comments.author: editor22uk
comments.body: Maybe its time we make hand illustrated slop so that it is distinguishable from ai slop 🤔

comments.author: Brewgazer
comments.body: Says senior stack dev but then says I used ai to make a browser game… if you have the dev experience you should know how to go in and fix the things you want fixed js

comments.author: WolvRs
comments.body: I dont design ui with ai, i use photoshop to make UI. simple

comments.author: HighDefinist
comments.body:
Wouldn't the solution be to simply "randomly change a bunch of things until the UI looks genuinely unusual"?

As in, sure, it might become slightly worse as a UI... but it should certainly be possible to find some compromises here.
